title: P1: Remote shell background processes survive connector shutdown and reconnect
detail:
Introduced by [dac779085094764c9f028d743bbd4f78f15c3f4e](https://github.com/SolenesInc/sigma/commit/dac779085094764c9f028d743bbd4f78f15c3f4e), authored by Victor Arias. Still present at eb70be3f4cae1840295ab07570968a8e35551204.

A remote Bash call can launch a dev server or watcher in the background with redirected stdio. The shell exits successfully while the child remains in its process group. Sigma removes the group record when the shell settles, so channel shutdown and the next hello have no record of the child to kill. The process can keep ports or files in use after reconnect, contrary to the target's close-kills and sweep behavior. See [exec.ts:212](https://github.com/SolenesInc/sigma/blob/eb70be3f4cae1840295ab07570968a8e35551204/packages/env/src/exec.ts#L212), [local.ts:667](https://github.com/SolenesInc/sigma/blob/eb70be3f4cae1840295ab07570968a8e35551204/packages/env/src/local.ts#L667), and [agent.ts:85](https://github.com/SolenesInc/sigma/blob/eb70be3f4cae1840295ab07570968a8e35551204/packages/env/src/agent.ts#L85) and [agent.ts:190](https://github.com/SolenesInc/sigma/blob/eb70be3f4cae1840295ab07570968a8e35551204/packages/env/src/agent.ts#L190).

A real `sigma exec` run against a throwaway target showed the same child PID before server shutdown, after shutdown, and after the next same-owner hello. A fresh reader independently reproduced the issue against real `sigma-env`. Both probes cleaned up their child. Review evidence is on attn seed `s-pvhs3r`.

Keep ownership of a live group after its shell exits, include it in teardown and the next sweep, and retire its record when the group is gone.
